title: New Research Finds That Revenue-Maximizing Top Tax Rate Likely Lower Than Previous Estimates
summary: A new paper shows raising top income tax rates on the current tax base may not yield as much revenue as previously estimated, due to opportunities to shift income to different tax bases within the tax code.

title: Property Tax Relief on the Ballot: Three Approaches, One Clear Winner
summary: This November, states across the country are asking voters to consider changes to their state constitutions to address the burden of rising property taxes.

title: A “Token Tax” Could Kill the Promise of AI
summary: If we want to ensure that AI raises economic growth, we shouldn’t be pursuing tax policies that are stuck in the past and represent some of the worst ideas from the early internet age.

title: How Much Does the US Government Lose to Tax Fraud?
summary: While the government will never close the tax gap or fully eliminate tax fraud, lawmakers and the IRS can institute several reforms to reduce the gap, including simplifying the tax code, increasing third-party information reporting, and coordinating anti-fraud efforts.

title: 2027 Tax Foundation Europe Gala
summary: Join us on Monday 27 September 2027 for Tax Foundation Europe’s second annual Gala. Hear from leading experts, network over dinner, and celebrate the pan-European tax policy community.

title: 2027 Tax Foundation Europe Conference
summary: Join us for Tax Foundation Europe’s 2027 Conference, where we will bring together leaders from the international tax community to discuss major tax topics, hear from top academics on new research, and more.

title: Could an Employer Compensation Tax Save Social Security?
summary: With Social Security insolvency rapidly approaching and policymakers exploring changes to benefits and taxation, Congress could look to base-broadening reforms like the ECT as a guide for how to think about taxing compensation and broadening the tax base.

title: Cigarette Taxes and Cigarette Smuggling by State, 2024
summary: Cigarette smuggling is costly for states. We estimate that the forgone revenue from smuggled cigarettes totaled more than $4.6 billion in 2024. California lost nearly $1.4 billion in cigarette excise tax collections, and New York missed out on more than $1.2 billion.

title: Spain’s Tax Competitiveness Has Declined Since 2018
summary: Under Spain’s current Social Democratic government, the country has fallen from 27th to 35th (out of 38 OECD countries) in the International Tax Competitiveness Index.

title: What Is Taxable Income? How It’s Calculated for Tax Filing
summary: Want to know how much you'll owe during tax filing season? Then you need to know your taxable income.
